rv.q: The overall effect is a striking blend of gritty realism and playful theatricality – an apt stage metaphor for Wilson's story of brutality and injustice shot through with fleeting moments of possibility.
I find it hard to believe that the play has been realised with such sensitivity and such power in those four decades since.
Bailey does little to offset the heaviness in the storytelling as the production drags beyond the three-hour mark.
Fences is a bruising, beautifully acted production about the stories we inherit, the stories we tell ourselves and the damage done when we mistake one for the other.
